chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Yazeed ibn Khalifa, and he is a man from the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, who said:

I heard him saying, 'I went to Medina, and Ziyad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Harithi was its governor. So I sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), entered, greeted him, and settled in my place. I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I am a man from Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guided me to your love and affection, O People of the Household.' He said to me, 'And how have you been guided to our affection, O People of the Household? By Allah, our love in Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b is scarce.'

He said, 'I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! I have a Khurasani slave who works as a bleacher, and he has four fellow countrymen. They invite each other every Friday, and the invitation falls upon one of them, so my slave's turn comes every five Fridays. He prepares Nabidh and meat for them. He said that when they finish eating the food and meat, he brings a bowl, fills it with Nabidh, then brings a clean jug. When he hands it to one of them, he says to him, 'Do not drink until you send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' Thus I was guided to your love through this slave.'

He said, 'So he said to me, 'Advise him well, and convey greetings from me to him, and say to him that Ja'far ibn Muhammad says to you: 'Look at this drink of yours which you are drinking. If a lot of it intoxicates, do not approach the little of it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden,' and said: 'Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, the little of it is forbidden.'

He said, 'So I went to Kufa and conveyed the greetings to the slave from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He wept, then said to me, 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) took such care of me that he conveyed greetings to me?' I said, 'Yes, and he told me to say to you: 'Look at this drink of yours which you are drinking. If a lot of it intoxicates, do not approach the little of it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden, and whatever a lot of it intoxicates, the little of it is forbidden,' and he advised me regarding you. Therefore go, for you are free for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.' The slave said, 'By Allah, it is a drink that will not enter my stomach as long as I remain in the world.'

key_terms.إِجَّانَة: Ijjana (a type of bowl or vessel)
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh (fermented drink, usually from dates or raisins)
key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ: Li-wajhi Allah (for the sake of Allah)

ai.seo_question: How did a slave's habit of serving Nabidh lead his master to the love of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of the principle of *kathir wa qalil* (abundance and scarcity) in determining the prohibition of wine, a key juristic distinction in Shia fiqh. The narrative highlights the social role of the Ahl al-Bayt in guiding even non-Arab servants, culminating in the slave’s voluntary manumotion as a sign of gratitude and spiritual elevation. It underscores the link between doctrinal adherence to the Prophet’s teachings and personal piety, where the slave’s vow to abstain reflects the transformative power of the Imam’s guidance.
